input: Get a second dental opinion on the crown quote

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is about price validation, treatment necessity, crown material choice, or all three changes what to ask the second dentist and what to compare.
Whether the user already has a second dentist in mind or needs to find one entirely changes the first steps of the plan.
Understanding what the original quote included (number of crowns, material, prep work) determines what documentation to bring and what questions to ask.
A deadline — such as a treatment window, insurance renewal, or pain urgency — dictates how quickly the second opinion must be secured.
Knowing whether the user has dental insurance affects which dentists are viable options and how costs will be compared.
The user may prefer a dentist of a specific type (e.g., prosthodontist vs. general dentist) or in a specific location, which narrows the search.
Clarifying what outcome would make this task feel resolved — confirming the price is fair, getting a cheaper alternative, or deciding whether the crown is even needed — defines when the task is done.

gold.taskTitle: Get a second opinion on dental crown quote
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to consult another dentist to verify whether the crown treatment plan and pricing they received is reasonable before committing.

questions.title: What specifically are you hoping to verify with this second opinion?
questions.description: Is the goal to check whether the crown is truly necessary, whether the quoted price is fair, whether the recommended material is right, or a combination?

questions.title: Do you already have a second dentist in mind?
questions.description: Knowing whether the user has a candidate dentist or needs to find one from scratch determines whether the first step is research or scheduling.

questions.title: What did the original quote include exactly?
questions.description: Details such as the number of crowns, crown material (porcelain, zirconia, metal), and any additional procedures like build-ups or extractions are needed to make a fair comparison.

questions.title: Is there a deadline by which you need to decide?
questions.description: A time pressure — due to pain, an expiring insurance benefit, or a dentist's scheduling window — will affect how urgently the second appointment needs to be booked.

questions.title: Are you covered by dental insurance for this treatment?
questions.description: Insurance coverage affects which dentists are in-network options and how the two quotes should be compared on an out-of-pocket basis.

questions.title: Do you have a preference for the type of dentist to consult?
questions.description: The user may want a specialist such as a prosthodontist rather than a general dentist, or may have a location or proximity preference that narrows the options.

questions.title: What outcome would make this task feel fully resolved for you?
questions.description: Understanding whether 'done' means finding a cheaper provider, simply confirming the original quote is fair, or deciding the crown is unnecessary shapes the entire plan.
